title: Nvidia’s $13 Billion Bet on Open AI
author: I
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Nvidia’s agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion is more than an AI deal. It is an attempt to control a distribution layer for open models—the platform where developers discover models, datasets, collaborate, fine-tune systems and deploy applications.

Hugging Face occupies a position in AI similar to GitHub’s role in software development. Its value is not limited to revenue or intellectual property; it lies in its community, tooling and place in developers’ workflows. Reuters reports that Nvidia plans to keep the service open and will not require customers to use Nvidia chips. That assurance matters because the platform serves developers working with competing accelerators and cloud providers.

For Nvidia, the purchase extends its reach beyond GPUs. The company already provides CUDA software, networking, systems and cloud services. Adding Hugging Face would give it a direct connection to model selection and deployment, allowing Nvidia to optimize popular workloads for its hardware and identify demand earlier. Open models could become another engine for GPU consumption as businesses seek customizable, cheaper alternatives to proprietary services from OpenAI and Anthropic.

The deal matters for the market because it brings a central piece of open AI infrastructure under the ownership of the dominant AI chip supplier. Nvidia’s scale could improve Hugging Face’s reliability, security and enterprise services. However, developers and regulators will watch for platform preferences: better performance on Nvidia hardware, privileged integration with its software stack, or governance decisions that disadvantage competitors.

The acquisition also signals that the competitive center of AI is shifting. Long-term power may belong not only to companies building the largest models, but to those controlling the tools, communities and infrastructure through which models reach users. Nvidia is betting that open AI will expand, and that owning its marketplace will reinforce demand across the Nvidia computing platform.
